text: Scusi, non sono di qui. / Sorry, I'm not from here.
why: The lesson's point is saying you didn't understand or don't speak much Italian. This example is fine Italian but shows neither; it only fits the notice's grammar aside about non before the verb, so it drifts the lesson toward negation in general.
fix: Use a line that shows the point, e.g. "Scusi, parlo solo un po' di italiano." / "Sorry, I only speak a little Italian."

text: Può scrivere il prezzo, per favore? / Could you write down the price, please?
why: The lesson teaches asking someone to repeat or speak more slowly. Asking someone to write something down is a different request, so this slips in a second point that no practice question uses.
fix: Replace with a repeat/slow-down line, e.g. "Scusi, può ripetere più piano?" / "Sorry, could you repeat that more slowly?"

text: No, sono qui per imparare l'italiano.
why: The model answer expects 'per imparare l'italiano', which no example or notice gives. The learner can't build it from the lesson.
fix: Ask something the examples cover, e.g. ask "Sei americano?", answer "Sì, sono americano."; or add an example with "Sono qui per imparare l'italiano."

why: 'In pensione' isn't given anywhere in the lesson before this question, so the answer depends on a phrase the learner hasn't been taught. (practice[2] then simply hands it back: 'Sei in pensione?' → 'Sì, sono in pensione.')
fix: Add an example with "Sono in pensione." or change the question to one answerable with taught words, e.g. "Sei qui in vacanza?" → "No, sono qui per lavoro." only if 'per lavoro' is shown in an example.

text: All three questions are 'Sei …?' answered with 'sono …'.
why: The how_to promises asking someone else with sei and è, but no practice question has the learner ask. Half the point is shown in examples and never practised.
fix: Make one question a prompt to ask, e.g. "Una signora anziana è nuova qui. Cosa chiedi?" → "È qui in vacanza?"

text: Italian says it in the present: sono, then da and the time.
why: The notice ties the pattern to sono only, but examples[3] uses studio and the practice answers use abito and studio. The notice doesn't explain what all the examples share: any present-tense verb plus da.
fix: "Italian says it in the present: the verb, then da and the time — sono qui da tre settimane, studio l'italiano da un mese. The time is still going, so it stays in the present."

text: Posso pagare io? / Can I get this one?
why: The lesson teaches posso pagare con la carta / in contanti. Putting io after the verb to mean 'my treat' is a second point the lesson never shows, so the learner can't arrive at this answer.
fix: Ask something the lesson covers, e.g. "Hai il bancomat. Cosa chiedi alla cassa?" → "Posso pagare con il bancomat?"
